title: Reject per-batch dirty-column dependency merge
impact: Fresh Dune evidence made repeated writer dependency merging a plausible exploit: identity sync runs every 2-5 seconds and executeBatch-updates three device columns plus two peer columns. A 64-bit pending-dependency mask safely merged each cached column only on the first actual table callback, preserving conditional triggers, FK cascades, no-row exits, and rollback/error cleanup. The mechanism is real at an extreme ceiling: 10,000 rows x 20 SET columns improves 64.5% / 60.9% across order-flipped worktrees. Rejected because the full-footprint 100-device + 100-peer product gate regresses 49.1% / 15.4% at p50 instead of improving at least 3%, and 1000+1000 is mixed at +9.1% / -2.0%. Runtime reverted; exact prototype at archive/exp-252. Reopen only for representative repeated UPDATE batches in the thousands of rows with materially wider SET lists, or a native profile proving this loop is material on a public product shape.
